question: Galvanisation protects iron from rusting by coating it with a thin layer of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc metal only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a metallurgical process used to protect **Iron** and **Steel** from **Rusting** by applying a thin, protective coating of **Zinc**.
 
• The process is highly effective because **Zinc** acts as a physical barrier between the metal and the atmosphere, preventing **Oxygen** and **Moisture** from reaching the surface of the **Iron**.
 
• The most common method utilized in industries is **Hot-dip galvanizing**, where the metal components are submerged in a bath of molten **Zinc** at temperatures typically around **450 degrees Celsius** (**842 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• A unique feature of this process is **Sacrificial Protection**; since **Zinc** is more chemically active (electropositive) than **Iron**, it corrodes in preference to the **Iron**, even if the coating is scratched or damaged.
 
• While other metals like **Nickel**, **Chromium**, or **Tin** can be used for coating (in processes like electroplating), the specific term **Galvanisation** refers exclusively to the application of **Zinc**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rusting of Iron**:

 
 
• **Rusting** is an oxidation reaction that occurs when **Iron** reacts with **Oxygen** in the presence of **Water** or **Moisture**.
 
• The chemical formula for rust is **Fe2O3.nH2O**, which is known as **Hydrated Iron(III) Oxide**. It is a reddish-brown flaky substance that weakens the structural integrity of the metal.
 
 
 
• **Other Methods of Rust Prevention**:
 
 
• **Painting and Greasing**: Provides a simple barrier to block **Air** and **Water**.
 
• **Alloying**: Mixing **Iron** with elements like **Chromium** (at least **10.5%**) and **Nickel** produces **Stainless Steel**, which is highly resistant to corrosion.
 
• **Anodizing**: Primarily used for **Aluminium**, it thickens the natural oxide layer on the metal surface.
 
• **Tinning**: Coating **Iron** or **Steel** with **Tin**, often used for food containers as **Tin** is non-toxic.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options**:
 
 
• **Silver**: It is an expensive precious metal and would be economically unviable for industrial rust protection.
 
• **Copper**: If used as a coating, it can actually accelerate the corrosion of **Iron** if the coating is breached because **Iron** is more reactive than **Copper**.
 
• **Nickel**: Used in **Electroplating** to provide a shiny finish and corrosion resistance, but it does not provide the same sacrificial protection as **Zinc**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Galvanisation** is named after the **Italian** scientist **Luigi Galvani**, who studied the effects of electricity on biological tissues, though the industrial coating process was developed later in the **19th Century**.
 
• In a **Galvanic Cell** setup, the **Zinc** acts as the **Anode** and the **Iron** acts as the **Cathode**, ensuring the base metal remains protected as long as the **Zinc** is present.
 
• Common applications of galvanized **Iron** include **Roofing sheets**, **Water pipes**, **Fencing**, and **Automotive body parts**.
